If you’re going for a repair, then go for it. But if the shopkeeper is suggesting you buy and install a new part, it’s better to visit a reputed shop or go directly to the official service center — that way, you’ll get value for your money.

My experience was somewhat similar.
When I went to a local shop to repair my bike's shock absorber, the mechanic suggested installing a new one from his shop and offered a 3-month guarantee, saying that if anything goes wrong, he would replace it with a new one. Unfortunately, within 3 months, a cracking sound started coming from the shock absorber.

So, I went back to show him the issue, expecting it to be replaced as promised. But instead, he just repaired the same shock absorber. After a few days, the same sound returned. I went again and asked him to replace it, but that time he changed his statement and said no one gives a guarantee like that. He repaired it again and even charged me for it.

Overall, I’m totally unsatisfied with this experience and regret not going to the service center in the first place. If I had installed a new shock absorber from the service center, I wouldn’t have faced all these issues.
